purpose: Per-origin network authorization, keyed by the NORMALIZED origin (scheme, host, effective port) and optionally narrowed to one candidate document. The network path resolves this BEFORE constructing a request.
rules: The key includes the effective PORT. https://host and https://host:8443 are different origins; a key of (scheme, host) alone would silently merge them.
An entry authorises only when its state is AUTO_FETCH_PERMITTED_BY_BASIS and its basisRef resolves through the basis registry with the ACQUISITION capability for this source, candidate and method.

A robots.txt Allow is one positive signal and never produces an entry here. Both hosts B1 refuses allow in robots.txt -- measured, HTTP 200, can_fetch True -- and both are refused, because their terms say otherwise.
Two entries whose keys collide, or whose scopes overlap ambiguously, REFUSE rather than resolve by precedence. Ambiguity that settles silently is how the wrong row becomes the authority.
emptinessNote: Deliberately empty at B1 closure. No origin is authorised for automated fetch. The pending portal request recorded in terms_acquisition_preflight.json is a REQUEST, not a grant, and produces no row here.
